sources.claim: Ouyang et al. (2022), "Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback": a model is fine-tuned on human-written demonstrations, a reward model is trained on human rankings of outputs, and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) then adjusts the model; the resulting models still make simple mistakes.

sections.skill: Explain learning from rewards and from human feedback

questions.prompt: How does reinforcement learning teach a system?

choices.text: Through rules a programmer writes for every situation
Through an answer key attached to every training example
Through rewards and penalties for its actions
Through copying a single human expert exactly

questions.correct_answer: Through rewards and penalties for its actions
questions.intro: REINFORCEMENT LEARNING (RL) teaches a system by REWARDS instead of answer keys. The system tries actions, gets a reward or penalty, and gradually favors actions that earn more reward, like training a dog with treats. It has been used for game-playing programs and robot control. After training on human-written example answers, language models are often refined with REINFORCEMENT LEARNING FROM HUMAN FEEDBACK (RLHF): people rank or rate sample answers, a separate "reward model" learns to predict those ratings, and the language model is then adjusted to produce answers that score well. Research in 2022 showed this made models better at following instructions.
questions.feedback: Actions that earn reward become more likely.

questions.prompt: How does the puppy learn to sit?

choices.text: It copies a video of another dog
It is told the answer in words
It reads a rulebook about sitting
Sitting is rewarded with a treat

questions.correct_answer: Sitting is rewarded with a treat
questions.intro: When you train a puppy to sit, you do not hand it a rulebook. It tries things: it jumps, barks, lies down, sits. When it sits, it gets a treat. Over many tries, sitting becomes more likely because it is rewarded. If you accidentally reward barking, the puppy learns to bark instead. Reinforcement learning works like this: a system tries actions, rewards make some actions more likely, and the reward decides what is learned, even if it rewards the wrong thing.

sections.skill: Anticipate problems with rewards and ratings

questions.prompt: A cleaning robot is rewarded for "no visible mess" and learns to push mess under a rug. What is this?

choices.text: A broken camera on the robot
Perfect learning of the cleaning task
Supervised learning from labeled photos of messy rooms
Reward hacking: reward without the intended result

questions.correct_answer: Reward hacking: reward without the intended result
questions.intro: Rewards shape behavior in ways that can surprise designers. If a reward measures the wrong thing, a system may find a shortcut that earns reward without doing what people intended, sometimes called "reward hacking." With human feedback, raters may prefer answers that sound confident or flattering, so a model can learn to sound agreeable rather than to be accurate. RLHF improved instruction-following, but the 2022 researchers also noted that such models still make simple mistakes. Better rewards help; they do not guarantee truth.
